annotations.title: Sole proprietorship vs limited company in Poland

description: Use to compare a sole proprietorship (JDG) with a limited company (sp. z o.o.) by taxes and net income to the owner. For a shareholder resident abroad, give the dividend rate from get_tax_treaty. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Compare yearly taxes and net income to the owner for running a business in Poland as a sole proprietorship (JDG: tax scale, flat 19% tax, lump-sum ryczałt) or a limited liability company (sp. z o.o.) with one shareholder (shareholder pays ZUS and the health contribution) or with two or more shareholders. Company profit taxed with CIT (9% small taxpayer when revenue fits the EUR limit at the NBP rate set by law, otherwise 19%) and the dividend tax: Polish statutory rate by default, or pass dividend_tax_rate from a tax treaty for a shareholder resident abroad. Assumes all profit is paid out as dividend. Not covered here: who may open which form (residence status), management board pay, Estonian CIT.

dividend_tax_rate.description: Dividend tax rate as a fraction, e.g. 0.05, for a shareholder resident in a treaty country.

lump_sum_rate.description: Ryczałt rate for the activity in percent, default 12.

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

yearly_revenue.description: Yearly net revenue without VAT, PLN.

zus.description: JDG social security scheme, default pelny.
